title: What do we do with the prisoners?
result: The Senate backed execution. Cicero had the five prisoners put to death that night.

lines.speaker: cicero
lines.text: We caught five men working with Catiline. He's got an army outside Rome. We need to decide what to do with the men in custody.

lines.speaker: caesar
lines.text: Take their property. Lock them up in towns that can hold them. We can do that without executing citizens on a Senate vote.

lines.speaker: cato
lines.text: Catiline's army is still out there. If they win, who's going to keep your prisoners locked up?

lines.speaker: caesar
lines.text: Okay, and next time a consul pulls up this vote and says Cicero got to do it, what are you going to tell him?

lines.speaker: cato
lines.text: Our ancestors didn't wait until an army was at the gates to act. Why are we acting like we've got all week?

lines.speaker: cicero
lines.text: You've heard both proposals. Senators, let's vote.
